rules: Keep total word count strictly between 85 and 100 words to ensure a fast-paced, high-retention delivery.
Narrator 1 handles the curiosity-inducing hook and the final question; Narrator 2 handles the dense technical explanation.
Place the pause/prediction prompt precisely at the 20-second mark to maintain rhythm.
Limit titles to 50 characters or fewer, starting with 'Why' or a 'Hidden/Secret' reveal.
Use visual transitions between scenes at least every 4 seconds to maintain active viewer engagement.
Ensure all technical explanations are delivered in plain, accessible language without jargon.
formats_now: The Hidden Engineering Reveal: Explaining the function of unseen design features (e.g., road safety, architecture).
Biological 'Why' Myths: Correcting common misconceptions about body processes using real-world science.
Micro-Process Breakdowns: Showing how everyday, mass-produced objects are actually manufactured.
Surprising Animal Adaptations: Exploring specific, counter-intuitive traits in nature.
hook_shapes: You think X does Y, but it is actually doing Z.
Ever wondered why X exists on Y? It is not for the reason you think.
This simple object X is actually a masterpiece of engineering, here is why.
Stop doing X; it is not actually helping, here is what is really happening.
stop_doing: Avoid using any 'How-to' or instructional advice, as these perform significantly worse than 'Why' explainers in our data.
Do not exceed 50 seconds in length, as retention drops sharply after this threshold.
Stop using overly long, complex sentences in the explanation phase; split them into two distinct clips.
experiment: Introduce a 'visual cliffhanger' (a high-contrast, zoomed-in image) at the 18-second mark right before the pause; success will be measured by a higher 'stayed_pct' compared to videos without this visual cue.
